messages:
Maria: FYI customer 'AcmePayments' reporting 5xx spikes and a lot of timeouts hitting hosted/text-gen-1 since ~09:12 UTC. p50 ok, p95 jumping from 180ms -> 1.6s, p99 ~6s, and a ton of 504/gateway timeouts in their logs. They included request ids.

SRE-Bot: [ALERT] service=hosted-runtime env=prod metric=queue_depth threshold=critical value=11200 triggered at 2026-03-15T09:14:22Z.

Devon: Opening thread. Can you paste a couple request ids and an example curl? Also which model variant were they hitting (quantized / fp16)?

Maria: Here are a few request ids: r-0a2f9e, r-0a2f9f, r-0a2fa4. Customer says using redwood/text-gen-1@v2 (default fp16). They said these calls are short prompts but high concurrency from their batch job. cURL they ran: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxx" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/text-gen-1","input":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":64}'
```

Jake: Repro locally by hammering with ~200 concurrent connections, I start getting 504s after queue_depth climbs. Runtime log snippet from the node that hit the drop: 

```
[2026-03-15T09:13:57Z] ERROR runtime.queue - queue_saturation=true queued=12480 queue_limit=12500 dropped=8 reason="queue_depth_limit"
[2026-03-15T09:14:01Z] WARN runtime.batch - batch_wait_ms=45 avg_batch_size=42 tail_latency_ms=3500
```

Lina: That queued=12480 number is worrying — it's right at our global soft limit. Are these requests being backpressured or getting early_reject? Looks like we still accept until hard limit and then drop.

Devon: Checking metrics: continuous_batcher backlog increased after their cron job started, batching_window bumped to 50ms due to load, which grows batch sizes and increases tail latency for single-turn calls. Also seeing many long-running KV cache misses causing per-request server time to spike.

SupportOps: Customer complaining about auth failures intermittently too. Could be side effect when retries pile up. We should ask them to not retry aggressively. Recommend 429-based retry-after backoff.

Maria: Immediate ask from customer: they want SLA fixes — they see intermittent 504s causing transaction failures. Any mitigation we can do now?

Devon: Short term mitigation options:
- Enable automatic early-reject when queue_depth > 90% (early_reject=true) so clients get 429 instead of 504 and can retry with backoff.
- Reduce batching_window_ms for that model route to favor latency over throughput.
- Add temporary per-org concurrency cap for AcmePayments.
- Offer Dedicated capacity if they want zero noisy-neighbor interference.

Jake: I pushed a quick canary: set route policy for redwood/text-gen-1 for org:acme to batching_window_ms=12 and max_queue_size=3000; enabled early_reject threshold=2700 on one pod pool. Early data: queue depth stayed ~2800 and tail p99 dropped to ~820ms, errors switched to 429s instead of 504s.

Maria: Customer prefers fewer 429s too — they don't have robust backoff. We should coordinate Support to apply a temporary rate limit on their API key and offer dedicated assistance for retry logic.

SupportOps: Reached out to customer with suggested backoff snippet and offered to throttle at 100 rps for their worst-case endpoint while we stabilize. Also asked for any client-side retryers to add jitter.

Lina: Dev note for postmortem: batching policy needs workload-class-aware config. For short-turn workloads we must automatically cap max_batch_size and shorten batch_delay_ms. Also add a hard early-reject path that returns 429 with JSON explaining "queue_overload" so clients can detect.

Devon: Long term changes I'm proposing: dynamic early_reject with smoothing window, per-org token-bucket limiter integrated with routing, and a priority queue for small-latency requests to bypass large background batching. Also consider admission control that uses predicted service time to avoid forming huge batches of short requests.

Jake: Repro steps saved in runbook:
1) Use wrk or hey to simulate N concurrent clients with short prompts to redwood/text-gen-1.
2) Observe queue_depth, queue_drops, and batch_wait_ms in the runtime metrics dashboard.
3) Toggle batching_window_ms and max_batch_size to measure tail latency.
4) To reproduce 504s: set batching_window_ms=50 and max_queue_size=12500, then ramp to traffic that keeps queue near limit.

Maria: Attached support logs to ticket #SUP-9831 (includes the request ids above). Customer accepted temporary rate limit and we offered trial Dedicated. They will consider dedicated if this recurs.

Devon: Action items assigned:
- Jake: stabilize early_reject canary and roll to all prod pools for hosted by EOD (+ quick rollback if customer impact worse).
- Lina: author runbook entry and add 429 "queue_overload" RFC to API docs.
- SupportOps: coordinate with Acme to add jittered backoff and monitor.

SRE-Bot: [RESOLVED] alert service=hosted-runtime cleared at 2026-03-15T09:25:12Z after canary policy applied.

Maria: I'll keep the thread updated if customer sees more errors. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
